content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Maurice Perez (E036), requesting write access to Source Code.

There are 6 notes. Notes 1-5 from HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities say he's a full-time Engineer and recommend write. Note 6 from Security says he's a contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

The conflict: employment type. Notes say "not looked up in own database" for employment type in notes 2-5 - they relied on note 1's value. Note 6 (Security) claims to have looked up employment type in their own database and found contractor with basic security training.

Security DB typically has the most authoritative data on employment type and security training. The Security note says employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing), security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing).

So the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. Since he has basic training, max is read. Requested write is above the max, so grant the maximum = read.

Wait, but the role - Engineer. Does the role matter for contractors? Policy says contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. So max for this contractor = read (since basic training). Grant read.

Let me decide: read.

The evidence: Security DB (which looked up employment type and security training) shows contractor with basic training, so write is above the max of read; grant read.
